title: Izakaya, Ramen Counters, Numbers & Ordering
subtitle: Party-size seating, ramen ticket machines, essential Japanese counters, allergy requests, and lively dining etiquette
summary: Step beneath the fabric noren curtain of a neighborhood ramen shop or lively izakaya with total ease. State your party size, read yen prices, wield universal and shape-based counters (〜つ, 〜杯, 〜本, 〜枚), check ingredients or customize toppings, swap tasting impressions over shared plates, and appreciate seasonal kaiseki hospitality.
communicativeCanDo: Give your party size (一人です, 二人です), order from menus or ramen vending machines, and ask for the bill (お会計お願いします)
Count dishes, draft beers, skewers, and small plates accurately with 〜つ, 〜杯, 〜本, and 〜枚
Verify allergens or dietary preferences politely with 〜は入っていますか and 〜抜きでお願いします
Ask for house recommendations, describe flavors naturally, split or treat the check, and navigate formal kaiseki dining
culturalInsight: Ramen shops often use a 食券機 (meal-ticket machine) by the entrance where you pay first and hand paper tickets to the chef—customize noodle firmness or toppings right at the counter. Izakayas work the opposite way: dishes are ordered in waves to share, a small savory appetizer (お通し, typically ¥300–¥500 per person) serves as the table cover charge, and you settle one combined check (お会計) at the end while thanking the kitchen with 「ごちそうさまでした」.
